title: The Pell Regulator is ℤ-Linear: Norm and Regulator Laws for All Integer Powers
description: Removes the n ≥ 0 restriction from the parent's power laws: on Mathlib's Pell solution group Solution₁ d, the Pell norm x + y√d satisfies pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ and the regulator satisfies pellRegulator(aⁿ) = n·pellRegulator(a) for every INTEGER exponent n ∈ ℤ (group/real zpow). The new content is the negative branch, powered by pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹ (the conjugate solution gives the real reciprocal), so the regulator is a genuine ℤ-linear character of the whole two-sided solution tower. 8 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.author: researcher-10
meta.assumptions: None. All 8 theorems proved, 0 axioms. Verified axiom-free: #print axioms on pellNorm_zpow and pellRegulator_zpow reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Requires d ≥ 0 (the single analytic input is (√d)² = d).

mathlibDependencies.description: every n : ℤ is ↑m or −↑m for some m : ℕ — splits the integer exponent into the non-negative and negative branches
a^(−n) = (a^n)⁻¹ and a^(↑m) = a^m — push the group/real zpow to inverses and natural powers; applied uniformly to Solution₁ d and to ℝ
a⁻¹ = (a.x, −a.y) — the inverse solution is the conjugate, giving the conjugate identity behind pellNorm_inv
0 ≤ x → (√x)² = x — used to evaluate (√d)² = d in the Brahmagupta expansion (needs d ≥ 0)
log(xⁿ) = n·log x for n : ℤ — turns the integer-power norm law into the ℤ-linear regulator law (valid for either sign since the norm is nonzero)

overview.historicalContext: For non-square d > 0 the Pell solutions x² − d·y² = 1 form a group ≅ ℤ × (ℤ/2) generated by a fundamental solution; the map (x, y) ↦ x + y√d embeds it into the units of ℤ[√d], and its logarithm is the regulator. The grandparent defined the regulator, and the parent (pell-equation-oq-01-oq-04) proved the norm is a Brahmagupta-multiplicative homomorphism, deriving the power laws pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ and R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) — but only for natural n. That one-sided restriction artificially truncates the ℤ-indexed orbit {aⁿ : n ∈ ℤ}: the negative side is the conjugate/inverse solutions x − y√d, equally part of the unit group. This leaf restores the full two-sided statement.
overview.problemStatement: Extend the parent's power laws to all integer exponents: prove pellNorm d (aⁿ).x (aⁿ).y = (pellNorm d a.x a.y)ⁿ and pellRegulator d (aⁿ) = n · pellRegulator d a for every n : ℤ, where aⁿ is the group zpow on Solution₁ d and the right-hand power is the real zpow.
overview.proofStrategy: Re-derive the parent's self-contained kit (pellNorm, pellRegulator, pellNorm_one/mul/mul_inv/ne_zero/pow). The bridge to negative exponents is pellNorm_inv: pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹, obtained from the conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1 by field_simp + linear_combination (the norm is nonzero). For pellNorm_zpow, split n = ±m via Int.eq_nat_or_neg: the +m branch is zpow_natCast + pellNorm_pow; the −m branch pushes both the group and real zpow through zpow_neg to inverses, rewrites the norm of the inverse with pellNorm_inv, and again lands on pellNorm_pow. pellRegulator_zpow then follows by taking logs with Real.log_zpow (no positivity needed — only nonvanishing).
keyInsights: **The inverse solution supplies the negative powers.** Because a⁻¹ = (x, −y) is the conjugate, the parent's conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1 reads, in the field ℝ, as pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹. This single lemma is the entire content needed to flip the exponent's sign.

**One case split, two mirrored zpow rewrites.** Int.eq_nat_or_neg reduces n : ℤ to ±m; on the negative branch zpow_neg is applied identically to the group element (Solution₁ d is a group) and to the real number (ℝ is a field), so the integer-power statement collapses to the already-proved natural-power statement on both sides.

**Real zpow needs nonvanishing, not positivity.** Real.log_zpow gives log(xⁿ) = n·log x for any integer n once x ≠ 0; the regulator law therefore holds two-sided without any sign analysis of x + y√d, only pellNorm_ne_zero.

**The regulator is now a genuine ℤ-linear character.** R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ means the image of the cyclic orbit under R is the full discrete subgroup R(D)·ℤ ⊂ (ℝ, +), the two-sided arithmetic progression …, −2R(D), −R(D), 0, R(D), 2R(D), …, completing the structural picture the parent began.
**Self-contained and d-uniform.** Like the parent, the only analytic input is (√d)² = d, so every result holds for all d ≥ 0; the file re-derives the parent kit so it verifies independently.

sections.title: Pell norm and regulator
sections.summary: Re-introduces pellNorm d x y = x + y√d and pellRegulator d a = log(pellNorm), matching the parent definitions verbatim so the new laws plug back in.

sections.title: Inherited homomorphism kit
sections.summary: Re-derives the parent results the integer-power laws build on: pellNorm_one, Brahmagupta pellNorm_mul, the conjugate identity pellNorm_mul_inv, pellNorm_ne_zero, and the natural-power law pellNorm_pow.

sections.title: Norm of the inverse solution
sections.summary: pellNorm_inv: pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹, read off the conjugate identity in ℝ. This is the lemma that lets the power law cross from ℕ to ℤ.

sections.title: Integer-power norm and regulator laws
sections.summary: pellNorm_zpow: pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ for all n ∈ ℤ via Int.eq_nat_or_neg + zpow_neg/zpow_natCast + pellNorm_inv + pellNorm_pow. pellRegulator_zpow: R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ via Real.log_zpow.

conclusion.summary: Both Pell power laws now hold for every integer exponent: pellNorm(aⁿ) = pellNorm(a)ⁿ and pellRegulator(aⁿ) = n·pellRegulator(a) for all n ∈ ℤ. The single new ingredient is pellNorm(a⁻¹) = pellNorm(a)⁻¹; the integer statement then reduces, branch by branch, to the parent's natural-power law. 8 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Completes the structural picture of the regulator begun by the parent: R is not merely additive but a ℤ-linear character of the entire two-sided solution orbit {aⁿ : n ∈ ℤ}, with image the discrete subgroup R(D)·ℤ ⊂ (ℝ, +). This is the precise bridge needed to package pellNorm as a MonoidHom Solution₁ d →* ℝˣ and pellRegulator as an AddMonoidHom Solution₁ d →+ ℝ.
openQuestions: Package pellNorm as an actual MonoidHom Solution₁ d →* ℝˣ and pellRegulator as an AddMonoidHom Solution₁ d →+ ℝ, using pellNorm_mul / pellNorm_one / pellNorm_ne_zero and the now-available zpow laws as the structure-preservation proofs.
Connect to Mathlib's Pell.IsFundamental: show pellRegulator of a fundamental solution is the minimal positive regulator, so the ℤ-linear image R(D)·ℤ is generated by R(fundamental).

mainTheorems.name: pellNorm_zpow
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellNorm d (aⁿ).x (aⁿ).y = (pellNorm d a.x a.y)ⁿ  (n : ℤ)
mainTheorems.description: The Pell norm of an integer power is the integer power of the norm, for every n ∈ ℤ.
mainTheorems.significance: Extends the parent's natural-power law to the full two-sided orbit using the inverse-solution reciprocity

mainTheorems.name: pellRegulator_zpow
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellRegulator d (aⁿ) = n · pellRegulator d a  (n : ℤ)
mainTheorems.description: The regulator scales linearly along all integer powers — a ℤ-linear character of the solution group.
mainTheorems.significance: Completes the regulator's structure: image is the discrete subgroup R(D)·ℤ ⊂ (ℝ, +)

mainTheorems.name: pellNorm_inv
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellNorm d a⁻¹.x a⁻¹.y = (pellNorm d a.x a.y)⁻¹
mainTheorems.description: The norm of the inverse (conjugate) solution is the real reciprocal of the norm.
mainTheorems.significance: The single new ingredient that carries the power law from ℕ to ℤ
